answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Mirror Rule. Each identity's action distribution is compared against its own prior epochs using a fixed divergence threshold; drift beyond it triggers reputation decay. Sybils must maintain costly long-horizon behavioural continuity, not just one-off registration. Enforcement spans a rolling river of epochs, so fresh identities cannot inherit history. A nebula score aggregates cross-epoch variance, making each maintained identity cost sustained compute and coordination to fake consistency.
